title: North African horse-word review
conclusion: Algeria is not unique: Moroccan Arabic and the Arabic-derived Kabyle form share the ʿawd set. Tunisia and the Benghazi Libyan reference use the ḥiṣān set. Hassaniya written فرس belongs to a separate faras set. Berber varieties retain distinct inherited sets and Arabic loans.

sources.title: Kossmann (2013), The Arabic Influence on Northern Berber, pp. 149–150: horse words and Arabic loans

Kossmann (2013), The Arabic Influence on Northern Berber, pp. 149–150: horse words and Arabic loans

regions.caveat: Rif also has akiđā, a distinct Moroccan Arabic loan from kid’ar, he-mule; no narrow synonym boundaries are inferred.
